Subject: Elysium - MSA/Order Form redlines (indemnity)

Jonas / Jordan,

Attached are Elysium's redlines to Redwood's standard MSA and Order Form. High-level summary of our asks below to keep the team aligned before legal and procurement dive in: 

- Full provider indemnity for third-party IP infringement arising from the service and any model output delivered to Elysium (no carveouts for model-derived content).
- Provider to control defense (no right to appoint external counsel by Elysium) and bear full defense costs; 10-day notice trigger for claims; no insurance offset.
- Aggregate cap requested: $5,000,000 (we understand you have lower caps typically but this is non-negotiable for our risk team unless we get stronger defense control and notice assurances).
- Carveouts requested for open-source / pre-existing customer data are narrow; we included suggested language.
- Evidence and preservation obligations, plus a tight SLA for producing artifacts (forensics, data samples) within 14 days.

We appreciate Redwood's cooperation here. Procurement (cc'd: Simon) will coordinate commercial if legal can get to a practical compromise. Can we target a call next week?

Regards,

Jonas — quick legal read and recommended commercial positions below. I attached a set of suggested redlines (KPark_suggested_redlines.docx) with tracked changes. High level: we can reach a workable compromise but we need to protect against customer misuse and open-source exposure.

Recommended positions (ranked):
1) Defense control: Redwood to have the primary right to defend IP claims where the claim arises solely from Redwood's models or service ("Provider Controlled Defense"), provided Redwood keeps Elysium reasonably informed and allows Elysium to engage counsel at its own expense. For mixed-cause claims, propose compulsory mediation/coordination.
2) Notice: keep a prompt-notice requirement but allow for "as soon as reasonably practicable" and explicit preservation duties; we cannot accept a 10-day hard bar — propose 30 days as a safe outer limit (unless claim was impossible to reasonably discover).
3) Cap: counter with $3,000,000 aggregate per 12-month period; provide rationale (market, insurance capacity). If customer insists on $5M, we can offer a phased cap increase tied to committed spend or insurance proof.
4) Insurance offset: allow offset only to the extent insurance proceeds are actually collected and applied to liability (no full set-off against Redwood's obligation).
5) OSS carveout: accept an express carveout for claims related solely to pre-existing open-source components or customer-supplied content; require Elysium to demonstrate provenance/evidence.
6) Evidence SLA: agree to reasonable cooperation and timely production; 14-day turnaround for routine artifacts is tight but we can commit to "good faith cooperation" and a prioritized triage process with an agreed evidence playbook.

Proposed path: send a short bulleted counter to Nadia that offers the items above; propose a 30-minute legal-to-legal call to clear the remaining definitional points (what counts as "model output" vs customer input).

Questions for sales (Ben/Jordan): any commercial levers (credits, cap ramp, longer term commitment) you want to offer to close?

-Kim
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
Attachment: KPark_suggested_redlines.docx

Subject: Redwood counter: Indemnity & defense (MSA / Order Form)

Nadia / Simon — thanks for the redlines. We reviewed internally and want to propose a compromise that should address Elysium's risk concerns while keeping obligations operationally viable for Redwood. Below are our counter positions (short form):

- Defense control: Redwood proposes primary defense for third-party IP claims that arise solely from Redwood's service (including model outputs generated without Elysium-provided infringing input). Redwood will have the right to select counsel and control defense; Elysium will have the right to participate with separate counsel at its own cost. For claims involving alleged customer misuse or combined causes, Redwood and Elysium will cooperate and engage in good-faith coordination; we propose a mediation step for unresolved control disputes.
- Notice: Elysium must provide notice to Redwood of any claim promptly and in any event within 30 days of becoming aware. Redwood will not be prejudiced by delays where notice could not reasonably be given.
- Cap: Redwood can accept an aggregate cap of $3,000,000 per 12-month period. As an alternative, we can offer a commercial trade — increase cap to $5,000,000 subject to a 12-month committed spend threshold (open to procurement discussion).
- Insurance offset: we will allow offset to the extent insurance proceeds are actually collected and applied to the indemnified loss (i.e., no unilateral full set-off).
- OSS / customer-supplied content: carveouts for open-source and Elysium-provided content where Elysium can demonstrate origin/provenance.
- Evidence & preservation: Redwood will follow a mutually agreed evidence-playbook and will prioritize production consistent with operational constraints; we commit to an expedited triage for high-priority forensic artifacts.

Attached is a tracked redline (Redwood_counter_redlines.docx) with proposed language. Would your team be available for a 30-minute legal call Thursday or Friday next week to resolve the remaining definitional items ("model output" vs customer prompt/fine-tune)? If procurement prefers to parallelize, happy to include them.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
